title: Minimum Threshold for Inversion Pairs Count
summary: Given an array of integers nums and an integer k, find the smallest integer min_threshold such that there are at least k inversion pairs with a threshold of min_threshold.
statement: Given an array of integers nums and an integer k, find the smallest integer min_threshold such that there are at least k inversion pairs with a threshold of min_threshold. An inversion pair is defined as a pair of indices (i, j) where i nums[j], and nums[i] - nums[j] <= min_threshold. If no such min_threshold exists, return -1.
constraints: nums has up to 10,000 positive integers and k is positive.
A qualifying inversion has i<j, nums[i]>nums[j], and difference at most the chosen threshold.
Return the smallest threshold producing at least k pairs, or -1 when the array has fewer than k inversions.
reference_solution:
def minimum_inversion_threshold(nums, k):
    values=sorted(set(nums));size=len(values)
    def count(threshold):
        from bisect import bisect_right
        bit=[0]*(size+1);total=0
        def prefix(index):
            result=0
            while index:result+=bit[index];index-=index&-index
            return result
        for value in nums:
            low=bisect_right(values,value);high=bisect_right(values,value+threshold)
            total+=prefix(high)-prefix(low)
            index=low
            while index<=size:bit[index]+=1;index+=index&-index
        return total
    high=max(nums)-min(nums)
    if count(high)<k:return -1
    low=1
    while low<high:
        middle=(low+high)//2
        if count(middle)>=k:high=middle
        else:low=middle+1
    return low

hints: The number of inversions whose difference is at most x is monotone in x, enabling binary search.
For each candidate x, scan left to right and use a Fenwick tree to count prior values in (value, value+x].
Reject when even the maximum difference has fewer than k pairs; otherwise binary-search the first sufficient x.
Fenwick range counts enforce index order and value bounds, while monotonicity proves the first sufficient threshold is minimal.
